input.quote: 19.4 For breach of Section 19.1 or 19.2, Vendor shall promptly re-perform, repair, or replace the nonconforming item at no charge. If Vendor cannot do so within a reasonable period, Customer may terminate the affected item and receive a refund of Fees paid for it.
input.rationale: Section 19 clears the fallback and substantially reaches the preferred position. Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel (19.1) with no time limit, and Services/Deliverables must materially conform to documentation and specifications; Deliverables carry a 90-day conformance warranty from the later of delivery or acceptance and Hosted Services must conform throughout the subscription term (19.2). Vendor also warrants compliance with Applicable Law and no malicious code (19.3). Remedies are repair/replacement/re-performance and, if Vendor cannot cure, termination plus refund of Fees paid (19.4), reinforced by the acceptance refund in 6.2. The disclaimer is mutual, limited to implied warranties, and expressly does not limit any express warranty or remedy (19.5), so it does not swallow the warranty; there is no "AS IS" language. The only shortfall against preferred is that the software/Deliverable conformance period is 90 days rather than 12 months (and malicious code is qualified to code intentionally introduced by Vendor) — sub-preferred points noted but not material deviations given the fallback is fully met.
